predecessors.name: Duchy of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Coburg, Ernest III's land, with Königsberg and Sonnefeld (from Saxe-Hildburghausen) and Callenberg and Gauerstadt (from Saxe-Meiningen); Saalfeld went to Meiningen

predecessors.name: Duchy of Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg
predecessors.text: Saxe-Gotha, the Gotha half of the extinct Gotha-Altenburg line (1,415 km2 in the 1914 table)

successors.name: Weimar Republic
successors.text: the state as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918 (the Free State of Coburg and the Free State of Saxe-Gotha)

ledger.x: 1826: the Treaty of Hildburghausen creates the Duchy of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha.
1826: Gotha joins Coburg under Ernest I.
1826: Königsberg and Sonnefeld pass from Saxe-Hildburghausen to Coburg.
1826: Callenberg and Gauerstadt pass from Saxe-Meiningen to Coburg.
1826: the Lichtenberg exclave stays with the new duke.

November 1918: 'In November 1918, Charles Edward, Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, was forced to abdicate'; infobox 'German Revolution: 18 November 1918'; 'the duchy became two independent states, the Free State of Coburg and the Free State of Saxe-Gotha.'

certainty.note: Two separate lands (Coburg in the south, Gotha in the north), 70 km apart, given by district names on the pages opened; no boundary survey is described.
